resources.string: Hear calls and talk with your iPhone’s own microphone and speaker. Android keeps call audio away from apps, so this needs Shizuku, a free app that gives Pairline extra access with your permission. Both phones also need to be on the same Wi-Fi.
This phone runs Android %1$s. Call audio on the iPhone needs Android 10 or later. Calls still ring on the iPhone, and you talk on this phone.
A free, open-source app from the Play Store or GitHub.
Update Shizuku to version 13 or later

In Shizuku, tap Start under “Start via Wireless debugging” and follow its steps. You turn on Wireless debugging yourself in Developer options; Pairline never does. After the phone restarts, start Shizuku again.
On Android 10, Shizuku is started from a computer once; the Shizuku app shows the command. After the phone restarts, start it again.
Shizuku asks whether Pairline may use it. Pairline uses it only for call audio and the call keypad, mute and speaker.
You said no before. Open Shizuku, go to Authorized apps and turn on Pairline.
The iPhone can hear your calls
This phone doesn’t let Shizuku capture call audio
Your voice from the iPhone can go into the call
This phone can’t feed audio into a call: you’ll hear calls on the iPhone and talk on this phone
When you answer on the iPhone, the call’s audio moves to the iPhone. Also turns on the keypad, mute and speaker from the iPhone.
Pairline learns what works on this phone from your answers after calls. This forgets them.
Call audio goes over your Wi-Fi, encrypted end to end. It’s never recorded or stored.
